cohort: Pregnant women who underwent induction of labor and delivered macrosomic neonates at a tertiary center between 2010 and 2020 were included, excluding those with non-cephalic presentation, prior cesarean section, or multiple pregnancies.
finding: No statistically significant differences were found in the rates of vaginal delivery or cesarean section, nor in maternal and neonatal secondary outcomes, between medical and mechanical methods of labor induction for macrosomic fetuses.
mod_finding: The choice of cervical ripening method (medical vs. mechanical) did not impact the mode of delivery (vaginal delivery or cesarean section).
birth_weight: macrosomic (implied to be >4000g based on context)
